facts.statement: Calamosaurus is a small theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period found on the Isle of Wight in England.
facts.quote: Calamosaurus (meaning "reed lizard") is a genus of small theropod dinosaur, from the Early Cretaceous of the Isle of Wight, England.

facts.statement: The genus is based on two cervical vertebrae collected by Reverend William Fox.
facts.quote: It is based on two cervical vertebrae (NHMUK PV R 901), collected by Reverend William Fox.

facts.statement: The fossils come from the Barremian stage of the Wessex Formation.
facts.quote: These fossils come from sedimentary rocks of the Wessex Formation and are Barremian in age.

facts.statement: Richard Lydekker renamed the genus Calamosaurus in 1891 after discovering the original name was preoccupied.
facts.quote: Upon realising his mistake, Lydekker promptly renamed it, creating the new combination Calamosaurus foxi (from the Latin sauros, "lizard") in 1891.

facts.statement: The classification of Calamosaurus has been controversial, with suggestions placing it in Compsognathidae or Ornithomimosauria.
facts.quote: The systematic position of Calamosaurus within theropods has been controversial, and placements within Compsognathidae and Ornithomimosauria have been suggested.

facts.statement: Recent research suggests affinities between Calamosaurus and the Tyrannosauroidea and Alvarezsauroidea.
facts.quote: More recently, researchers have suggested affinities with the Tyrannosauroidea and Alvarezsauroidea.

facts.statement: A 2026 paper tentatively identified Calamosaurus foxi as a basal alvarezsauroid.
facts.quote: A paper from 2026 tentatively identified C. foxi as a basal alvarezsauroid.

facts.statement: The two holotype cervical vertebrae are approximately 40 millimeters in length.
facts.quote: Both of the holotype Calamospondylus cervical (neck) vertebrae are about 40 mm in length.

facts.statement: The cervical vertebrae have very strongly reduced epipophyses, suggesting a small and lightly built head.
facts.quote: The cervical vertebrae were at one point interpreted as lacking epipophyses entirely, suggesting a small, lightly built head; whilst they are indeed present, they are very strongly reduced.

facts.statement: Calamosaurus lived in a floodplain environment with river and lake deposits during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The holotype of Calamosaurus heralds from the Wessex Formation. Sedimentological data suggests that the depositional environment of the Wessex Formation was a floodplain intersected by fluvial (river) and lacustrine (lake) deposits.

facts.statement: The environment experienced frequent wildfires that likely stifled the growth of dense gymnosperm forests.
facts.quote: Burned plant and insect material and fusain suggests that the environment experienced frequent wildfires, stifling for the most part the dense growth of gymnosperms.

facts.statement: The local flora consisted mainly of low ground cover like pteridophytes, with occasional conifers, cycads, and tree ferns.
facts.quote: Much of the flora of the formed of low ground cover, consisting primarily of pteridophytes, with occasional stands of conifers, cycads and the tree fern Tempskya.

facts.statement: Some authors consider Calamosaurus a nomen dubium due to its fragmentary nature, though this is not a universal view.
facts.quote: Some authors have opted to relegate Calamosaurus to the status of a nomen dubium due to its fragmentary condition and ambiguous taxonomy, although this view is not universal.

facts.statement: In 2011, Darren Naish supported the genus's validity based on similarities to Dilong paradoxus but cautioned against adding more remains due to its fragmentary state.
facts.quote: In 2011, Darren Naish supported the validity of the genus, and noted similarities with the Chinese taxon Dilong paradoxus that are indicative of a basal position within Tyrannosauroidea, though did caution against the assignment of further remains to the genus considering its fragmentary state.

facts.statement: Calamosaurus is classified within the family Coeluridae.
facts.quote: familia: Coeluridae

facts.statement: Calamosaurus foxi is the only known species of the extinct theropod dinosaur genus Calamosaurus.
facts.quote: Calamosaurus foxi (gr. "lagarto quilla del rev. William Fox") es la única una especie conocida del género extinto Calamosaurus de dinosaurio terópodo

facts.statement: Calamosaurus lived during the early Cretaceous, approximately 130 to 112 million years ago in the Barremian stage in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 130 a 112 millones de años, en el Barremiense en lo que es hoy Europa

facts.statement: The type specimen of Calamosaurus consists of two cervical vertebrae (BMNH R901) collected by Reverend William Fox from the Wessex Formation on the Isle of Wight, England.
facts.quote: Encontrado en la Formación Wessex de la Isla de Wight, Inglaterra se basa en dos vértebras cervicales,BMNH R901, recogidas por el Reverendo William Fox

facts.statement: Richard Lydekker named the species Calamospondylus foxi when he cataloged Reverend Fox's fossil collection.
facts.quote: Richard Lydekker se topó con estos huesos al catalogar la colección del reverendo Fox y nombrado por este Calamospondylus foxi

facts.statement: Richard Lydekker renamed the species to Calamosaurus in 1891.
facts.quote: Lydekker lo renombró a su actual nombre en 1891

facts.statement: As a basal coelurosaurian, Calamosaurus was likely small, agile, bipedal, and carnivorous.
facts.quote: Como un celurosauriano basal, Calamosaurus probablemente fue pequeño, ágil, bípedo y carnívoro

facts.statement: Adult Calamosaurus individuals are estimated to have been between 3 and 5 meters long.
facts.quote: Se ha estimado que el tamaño de un individuo adulto pudo oscilar entre los 3 y 5 metros de largo

facts.statement: Paul Turner discovered a dorsal vertebra near Grange Chine on the Isle of Wight in 2002.
facts.quote: En 2002 Paul Turner encontró una vértebra dorsal cerca de Grange Chine en la Isla de Wight

facts.statement: Oliver Mattsson later discovered an associated fragment of a partial tibia and metatarsal attributed to Calamosaurus.
facts.quote: Un fragmento asociado de tibia parcial y metatarsiano fue descubierto posteriormente por Oliver Mattsson

facts.statement: Local fossil hunter Kai Bailey collected another specimen referred to Calamosaurus in 2014.
facts.quote: Otro espécimen referido a Calamosaurus fue recogido por el cazador de fósiles local Kai Bailey en 2014

facts.statement: Local fossil hunter Dave Badman found a cervical vertebra of a Calamosaurus near Chilton Chine on the Isle of Wight.
facts.quote: El cazador local de fósiles Dave Badman encontró una vértebra del cuello de un Calamosaurus cerca de Chilton Chine en la Isla de Wight

facts.statement: Modern revisions classify Calamosaurus as a dubious theropod, though it remains a potentially valid coelurosaurian.
facts.quote: Revisiones modernas lo colocan como un terópodo dudoso, aunque es un celurosauriano potencialmente válido

facts.statement: In 2007, D. Naish and D. M. Martill considered Calamosaurus to belong within Tyrannosauroidea.
facts.quote: En 2007 D. Naish y D. M. Martill consideraron a Calamosaurus dentro de Tyrannosauroidea

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Calamosaurus as Tyrannosauroidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Tyrannosauroidea

facts.statement: Calamosaurus is classified under the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Calamosaurus is Calamosaurus foxi.
facts.quote: Type species: Calamosaurus foxi

facts.statement: The time range for Calamosaurus is the Barremian to Aptian stages, from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The name Calamosaurus means 'reed lizard' and refers to the slender and lightweight build of the vertebrae.
rejected.quote: The name derives from the Ancient Greek kalamos ('reed', 'reed pen') and spondylos ('vertebra') and hints at the slender and lightweight build of the vertebrae.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'the slender and lightweight build of the vertebrae'

rejected.statement: Researchers estimated in 2001 that Calamosaurus may have reached a body length of 3.5 meters.
rejected.quote: In 2001, Darren Naish, Steve Hutt, and David Martill estimated that Calamosaurus may have reached a body length of 3.5 m.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'that Calamosaurus may have reached a body length'

rejected.statement: Makovicky et al. (2026) interpret Calamosaurus foxi as an alvarezsauroid, a hypothesis that contrasts with its traditional classification.
rejected.quote: the authors also interpret the Late Jurassic theropod vertebra described by Makovicky (1997), the theropod astragalus YPM 9163 from Como Bluff (Morrison Formation, Wyoming, United States; formerly referred to Coelurus fragilis) and Calamosaurus foxi as alvarezsauroids
